forces.title: Hybrid AC/DC Architectures Enhance Battery Integration and Efficiency
forces.description: The global shift towards hybrid AC/DC power architectures, driven by natively DC energy sources like solar and loads such as data centers and EVs, represents a significant tailwind for battery energy storage. This integration minimizes energy conversion losses and optimizes the use of solar and battery assets, which are increasingly critical in industrial, commercial, and residential settings in Europe. This structural change streamlines power management, making battery storage more efficient and economically attractive, especially as power density demands increase.
forces.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

forces.title: UK Data Centre Growth Drives Demand for Behind-the-Meter Storage
forces.description: The rapid expansion of data centers in the UK, particularly in grid-constrained areas like Northern Virginia and Europe, is a major tailwind for energy storage. These facilities face significant power access and grid connection delays, creating strong demand for behind-the-meter generation, storage, and flexibility solutions. Policy changes allowing data centers to use such assets as a bridge or permanent alternative to grid reinforcement incentivize battery deployment, contributing to system value by absorbing additional demand and potentially reducing household electricity bills.
forces.source_title: To Cut Electricity Bills, Britain Needs to Use More, Not Less

forces.title: Gigafactory Construction Delays Impede Battery Supply Chain Scale-Up
forces.description: Delays in the delivery of battery gigafactories, averaging six to nine months, pose a significant risk to the energy storage sector. These delays, often caused by immature product and process designs, pursuit of unproven technologies, and ineffective ecosystem partner management, result in substantial financial impacts and disruptions across the value chain. As battery demand for utility-scale BESS grows and supply chains localize, timely gigafactory delivery is critical for maintaining competitive advantage and meeting increasing market needs, making these delays a material headwind.
forces.source_title: Gigafactory delivery on time: Solving the SOP delay challenge

forces.title: Battery Energy Storage System Costs Declining Rapidly Globally
forces.description: Utility-scale battery installation costs have dropped by over half since 2022 and are projected to fall by another 50% over the next decade. This significant structural change is primarily driven by technological advancements, such as the shift to lower-cost lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry, and manufacturing improvements by Chinese producers. These declining costs make solar combined with BESS increasingly attractive, enhancing the economic viability and deployment pace of energy storage projects globally, despite potential tariffs and trade barriers impacting regional prices.
forces.source_title: Solar power: From intermittent sunshine to reliable power

forces.title: UK Battery Revenue Streams Shift from Ancillary Services to Energy Trading
forces.description: The UK's battery energy storage market is undergoing a structural change where revenue generation has shifted significantly from ancillary services to energy trading. This evolution is a direct result of increased storage deployment and market maturity. Operators are now optimizing across various revenue streams, including supplying electricity when prices are higher and participating in capacity markets. This shift indicates a more sophisticated and competitive market environment, requiring advanced dispatch and bidding strategies, potentially enabled by AI, to maximize profits and returns on battery assets.
forces.source_title: Solar power: From intermittent sunshine to reliable power

forces.title: AI-Enabled Dispatch Strategies Boosting Battery Profitability
forces.description: The adoption of AI-enabled dispatch and bidding strategies is a significant upside driver for battery energy storage operators. These technologies can lift battery profits by more than 20% by facilitating real-time decisions on when to charge, discharge, and sell into power markets. As solar penetration increases and market volatility grows, sophisticated AI tools enable operators to shape output, manage price exposure, and match customer demand more closely, moving beyond simply owning a low-cost asset to actively optimizing its value generation in complex energy markets.
forces.source_title: Solar power: From intermittent sunshine to reliable power

forces.title: Grid Access Constraints Hinder BESS Integration and Monetization
forces.description: Limited transmission capacity, grid congestion, and slow interconnection processes are becoming critical constraints and a key risk for energy storage projects, particularly in markets like the United States where median wait times can be 60 months. Even with attractive solar and storage costs, these grid access issues can significantly delay projects and impede the effective integration and monetization of BESS. For policymakers, addressing these barriers through accelerated permitting, transmission infrastructure expansion, and market mechanisms rewarding flexibility and storage is paramount.
forces.source_title: Solar power: From intermittent sunshine to reliable power

forces.title: UK Government Funding Supports Domestic Battery Installations
forces.description: The UK government's commitment to funding schemes provides a significant tailwind for domestic battery energy storage. The Warm Homes Plan allocates £1 billion annually to support low-income households for solar PV and batteries, while £2 billion in low and zero-interest consumer loans assists homeowners with these costs. These incentives aim to reduce household electricity consumption and energy bills, driving uptake of home battery systems. This direct financial support lowers consumer barriers to adoption and accelerates the deployment of decentralized energy storage solutions.
forces.source_title: Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament

forces.title: LDES Scheme Drives Major Long-Duration Storage Project Pipeline
forces.description: Ofgem's Long Duration Energy Storage (LDES) scheme is a strong tailwind for the UK energy storage sector, particularly for lithium-ion batteries. In September 2025, 77 projects totaling 28.7 GW progressed to the Project Assessment Stage. This substantial pipeline indicates significant investment and development in long-duration storage, which is critical for balancing the grid and integrating renewables over longer periods. The anticipated award decisions will further catalyze the deployment of these large-scale projects, underpinning the UK's energy transition goals.
forces.source_title: Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament

forces.title: National Wealth Fund Invests in UK Battery Manufacturing
forces.description: The National Wealth Fund's commitment of £5.8 billion by 2030/31 towards battery manufacturing and electric vehicle supply chains is a significant tailwind. While explicitly mentioning EV supply chains, the investment in 'battery manufacturing' broadly supports the development of a domestic industrial base for battery cells, which are fundamental to both EV and grid-scale energy storage systems (BESS). This funding aims to reduce import dependence, foster local champions, and secure supply chains, thereby strengthening the foundation for the UK's energy storage sector.
forces.source_title: Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament

forces.title: UK Regulatory Framework Lacks Incentives for Co-located Storage
forces.description: Current UK regulatory frameworks, including the Contracts for Difference (CfD) model, were not designed with energy storage in mind and offer limited incentives for storing excess power, particularly for co-located offshore wind and storage projects. This regulatory gap acts as a headwind, undermining the economics of valuable solutions that could reduce curtailment and unlock commercial value for offshore wind. Without appropriate reforms, this lack of incentive slows the transition of offshore co-located storage from a niche application to core system infrastructure.

forces.title: Modular Manufacturing Driving Offshore Storage Cost Reductions by 2040
forces.description: The projected 40% reduction in offshore storage costs by 2040, driven by modular manufacturing, represents a significant structural change. This cost evolution is crucial for transforming offshore co-located storage from a niche solution to a mainstream asset. Lower costs will enhance the economic viability of integrating storage systems with offshore wind farms, enabling them to absorb excess generation, smooth output, and improve revenue certainty. This development is key to scaling energy storage alongside deep-water wind projects, contributing to UK's net-zero ambitions.

forces.title: Storage Repetitive Re-Trading Raises Consumer Costs, Hinders Wind Integration
forces.description: Repetitive re-trading (RRT) by storage assets, driven by national price signals, is identified as a material feature of GB electricity markets, costing consumers £136.3 million from November 2024 to October 2025. This 'flip-flopping' behaviour, where batteries buy and sell power without changing state of charge, means storage may not effectively absorb excess wind, posing a key risk to wind integration and overall system efficiency. This inefficiency could undermine the intended benefits of storage in a renewables-led system.

forces.title: Potential Market Reforms Threaten Storage Net Revenues and Investability
forces.description: Upcoming policy reforms, including Balancing Mechanism (BM) pricing changes, non-firm access, and hybrid dispatch, represent a key risk to the financial viability of energy storage projects in GB. Modelling suggests these reforms could materially reduce expected storage net revenues by 27% to 92%. While aimed at improving efficiency and wind integration, such significant revenue reductions could deter investment in new storage capacity, jeopardizing the sector's growth and its ability to provide flexibility for a renewables-led system. Striking a balance between benefits and investability is crucial.

forces.title: Growing Battery and Pumped Storage Enhancing Grid Flexibility
forces.description: The ongoing growth of battery storage and year-on-year improvement in pumped storage availability are strong tailwinds for the GB electricity system. These assets are enhancing the potential to increase transmission system demand and provide significant within-day flexibility, including vital system services like fast-acting frequency response. Particularly during extended low demand periods, the increasing capacity and efficient operation of these storage technologies are crucial for balancing supply and demand, reducing reliance on inflexible generation, and supporting a secure, low-carbon network.

forces.title: Emergence of Grid-Forming Battery Technology for System Stability
forces.description: The connection of Great Britain’s first grid-forming battery site and the development of grid-forming inverter technology represents a significant structural change in energy storage. Grid-forming inverters enable renewables like batteries to actively control current and voltage fluctuations, behaving similarly to synchronous power stations. This innovation reduces reliance on conventional generators for critical transmission system services, improves system stability, and enhances resilience, thereby lowering costs for consumers and accelerating the transition to a clean power system.

forces.title: Integrated EV Battery Production and Recycling Supply Chain in UK
forces.description: The development of an integrated supply chain in southwest England for EV battery production and recycling, including a gigafactory poised to meet nearly half of UK EV battery demand by 2035, is a significant tailwind for the broader battery sector. While focused on EVs, this industrial base for battery manufacturing and recycling establishes critical capabilities and infrastructure that can also support the BESS market. This local ecosystem fosters collaborative resilience and reduces dependence on external suppliers, strengthening the domestic battery industry's foundation.

forces.title: Strong Investor Interest Drives UK Energy Storage Sector Growth
forces.description: Robust investor interest in UK energy storage, with 70% of surveyed investors expressing interest, acts as a powerful upside driver. This strong market confidence, largely attributed to the clear scalability of battery storage technologies, indicates a healthy appetite for capital deployment in the sector. This enthusiasm facilitates financing for new projects, supports innovation, and enables the expansion of storage capacity crucial for the UK's energy transition, making energy storage one of the most attractive opportunities in the renewable energy landscape.

forces.title: Increased Need for Storage Due to Renewable Intermittency
forces.description: The increasing prominence of intermittent renewable energy sources like wind and solar creates a rising and critical need for large-scale battery storage and other flexible technologies in the UK. As the energy mix diversifies, energy storage provides essential real-time balancing to respond quickly to fluctuations in supply and demand. Batteries are vital for storing surplus renewable electricity and releasing it when generation falls short, thereby smoothing out peaks and troughs and ensuring stable energy supplies during the transition to Net Zero.

viewpoints.title: Hybrid AC/DC Power Architectures Boost Battery Integration Efficiency in Europe
viewpoints.description: BCG Global posits that hybrid AC/DC power architectures are becoming essential, particularly in Europe, for high-density applications like data centers, industrial plants, and commercial buildings. This shift is driven by the native DC nature of new energy sources (solar, batteries) and loads (data centers, EVs). Integrating batteries more efficiently reduces conversion losses, optimizes solar use, and leverages scarce grid connections. Although residential cases are not yet compelling, policy shifts and time-of-use tariffs are expected to improve the economics, making batteries more central to energy management.
viewpoints.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

viewpoints.title: Solar+BESS Performance Hinges on Integration and Monetization Beyond Cost
viewpoints.description: McKinsey asserts that the profitability of solar PV projects, especially those paired with Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), increasingly depends on effective integration, monetization strategies, and volatility management, rather than solely on achieving low generation costs. As solar penetration rises and wholesale prices become more volatile, the ability to store electricity and discharge it during higher-priced periods, along with matching supply to demand, is crucial. This signifies a strategic shift for developers to maximize value from their assets.
viewpoints.source_title: Solar power: From intermittent sunshine to reliable power

viewpoints.title: UK Battery Storage Progress on Track to Meet Ambitious Targets
viewpoints.description: The Climate Change Committee (CCC) reports that the UK is making good progress in deploying grid-connected battery storage, with capacity additions currently on track to achieve government targets. A record 2 GW of new grid-connected battery storage was installed in Great Britain in 2025, contributing to a 2024 capacity of 6.8 GW. The significant pipeline of projects, including those under the Long Duration Energy Storage (LDES) scheme, supports the ambition to reach 23-27 GW of short-duration capacity by 2030, reinforcing confidence in the sector's growth.
viewpoints.source_title: Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament

viewpoints.title: UK's Ambitious Storage Targets Signal Strong Growth Trajectory by 2030
viewpoints.description: Deloitte UK highlights the UK's ambitious targets for energy storage, aiming for 27–33 GW of combined long-duration and battery storage capacity by 2030, a significant increase from the current 7 GW. This outlook underscores a strong growth trajectory and policy support for the energy storage sector. The firm's analysis implicitly conveys a positive stance on the sector's potential, driven by national decarbonisation goals and the need for grid flexibility to integrate increasing renewable energy sources.

viewpoints.title: Offshore Co-located Storage Poised for Significant Role by 2040
viewpoints.description: Xodus, in collaboration with Subsea7, identifies offshore co-located energy storage as an emerging solution for reducing curtailment and unlocking commercial value in the UK and wider Northern Europe. While currently a niche application, it is projected to become a valuable part of the energy system by 2040. Placing storage systems on the generator side of the transmission boundary can absorb excess generation, smooth output, and improve revenue certainty, thereby addressing grid bottlenecks caused by rapid offshore wind deployment outpacing grid upgrades.

viewpoints.title: GB Storage Markets Need Reforms to Address Inefficient 'Repetitive Re-Trading'
viewpoints.description: FTI Consulting, cited by OEUK, points out that national price signals in Great Britain incentivize battery storage assets to engage in 'repetitive re-trading' (RRT). This involves buying and selling power in wholesale and balancing markets without changing the state of charge, leading to inefficiencies and significant costs for consumers (£136.3m from Nov 2024 to Oct 2025). The firm argues that reforms are necessary to ensure storage effectively supports wind integration and remains investable, despite potential material reductions (27-92%) in net revenues from such policy changes.

viewpoints.title: Battery and Pumped Storage Critical for UK Grid Flexibility and Stability
viewpoints.description: NESO expresses confidence in its ability to operate a rapidly changing electricity system safely and efficiently, with battery storage and pumped hydro storage increasingly playing a critical role. These assets enhance transmission system demand potential and provide significant within-day flexibility, including fast-acting frequency response. NESO is developing new services and market designs to integrate these flexible resources, highlighting their importance in balancing supply and demand, especially during periods of low demand and high renewable generation, to ensure secure, low-cost, and low-carbon system operation.

viewpoints.title: Large-Scale Battery Storage Essential for Balancing UK's Intermittent Renewables
viewpoints.description: OEUK emphasizes the growing and critical need for large-scale battery storage and other flexible technologies to balance the UK's energy system. As renewable sources like wind and solar become more prominent, their inherent intermittency creates demand for assets that can respond quickly to supply and demand fluctuations. Batteries are highlighted for their ability to store surplus electricity during high renewable output and release it when generation is low, thereby smoothing peaks and troughs and complementing traditional fossil fuels in maintaining real-time system stability.

viewpoints.title: Energy Storage Identified as Top Investment Opportunity in UK Energy Transition
viewpoints.description: Deloitte UK reports that energy storage, particularly battery storage, is considered one of the most attractive investment opportunities in the UK's energy transition. Survey data indicates that 70% of investors are interested in energy storage technologies, citing their clear scalability. This strong investor confidence positions the sector favorably for continued growth and development. The demand for grid infrastructure and mature supply-side technologies also contributes to this positive outlook, aligning energy storage with key areas of interest for capital deployment.

demand_drivers.description: The automotive industry's transition to electric powertrains is driving increased demand for batteries.
Rapidly increasing power demand stresses grids, and electricity networks need more capacity from intermittent renewables, driving demand for utility-scale battery storage.

market_sizing.methodology: Global market forecast for high-performance batteries, including EV and utility-scale BESS, rising from 1.6 TWh today.
market_sizing.source_title: Gigafactory delivery on time: Solving the SOP delay challenge

demand_drivers.description: Increased deployment of solar PV necessitates battery storage to manage intermittency and provide reliable power, driving BESS investment.

market_sizing.methodology: Global investment projection for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), reflecting a rapid increase from $80 billion in 2025 and growth of solar PV.
market_sizing.source_title: Solar power: From intermittent sunshine to reliable power

demand_drivers.description: Growth in power and gas trading is shifting towards products that price in flexibility, such as Flexibility Purchase Agreements (FPAs), where BESS plays a key role in optimization.

market_sizing.methodology: Capacity contracted in Europe via Flexibility Purchase Agreements (FPAs), predominantly originating battery energy storage systems. This figure compares to less than 5 GW in previous years.
market_sizing.source_title: Power, Gas, and LNG Trading: Racing to Compete in the Coming Decade

demand_drivers.description: Ambitious government targets for decarbonizing the energy system necessitate a significant increase in storage capacity to integrate renewables and ensure grid stability.

market_sizing.methodology: Current operational capacity of both long-duration and battery storage in the UK. The target is 27-33 GW by 2030.

demand_drivers.description: The UK government's targets for low-carbon electricity supply and electrification drive the need for substantial battery storage capacity to balance the grid and integrate renewables.
A significant number of battery storage projects are in the connections queue, indicating future deployment will likely meet government ambitions.

market_sizing.methodology: Official data for grid-connected battery capacity in Great Britain. An estimated 2 GW was installed in 2025. The government's ambition for short-duration capacity is 23-27 GW by 2030, requiring an average annual deployment of 2.7-3.4 GW.
market_sizing.source_title: Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament

demand_drivers.description: The transition to a decarbonized energy system requires storage solutions that can balance seasonal fluctuations and provide resilience over extended periods, which LDES aims to address.

market_sizing.methodology: Potential capacity from 77 projects that progressed to the Project Assessment Stage of Ofgem's Long Duration Energy Storage (LDES) scheme in September 2025. A significant portion of this capacity is expected to be lithium-ion batteries.
market_sizing.source_title: Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament
